source.interpretation: Noncritical failure becomes critical when NCFTL is reached and active repair has not started. NCFTT selects calendar or operational exposure. A pending noncritical task can leave a system available for a new mission; escalation can abort mission operation and reprioritize waiting for spares/resources. Dictionary uses OPERATION as the NCFTT choice; manual prose calls it OPERATIONAL.

predeclared_hypotheses_not_outcomes: Both arms retain the accepted parent's first noncritical in-mission LRU fault near h9.8829 and complete the h10 mission before the 0.2-hour limit.
With no local spare, the noncritical replacement task waits and active repair has not started at h10.
Calendar NCFTL expires near h10.0829 between missions; criticality escalation reinitiates spare/resource waiting and prevents an unchanged noncritical h20 mission start.

Operational NCFTL retains about 0.1171 hours exposure at h10 and does not advance while idle; if the aircraft takes the h20 mission with repair still pending, escalation is expected about 0.0829 hours into it, with abort and reprioritized repair.

Native event times, same-item repair/backorder handling, mission outcomes, result bins and terminal readiness are to be determined from sealed raw output; a failed hypothesis constrains acceptance rather than being rewritten.
native_acceptance_gates: Frozen source hashes and exact deltas verified before native execution.
Session-0 SSH, host-wide mutex, active GUI PID 13340 identity, unchanged installed executable/manual/dictionary and zero conversion errors.
All authored row-containing tables import/export identically; valid nonempty SXO and event/result reports.
Independent read-only replay distinguishes calendar and operational escalation by individual event sequence, mission disposition, repair/stock queue and aligned report/terminal ledgers.
If native semantics differ, report a bounded counterexample or restriction without silently upgrading the planned claim.
